headline: Anthropic's S-1 reveals $16.3B revenue, $80.7B loss ahead of IPO
summary: Anthropic's draft S-1 shows a booming $16.3 billion revenue in H1 2026, alongside an $80.7 billion net loss, largely due to non-cash adjustments, as it prepares for one of the year's largest IPOs.
details: Anthropic's draft S-1 reveals a company with staggering growth and massive losses. The AI lab generated $16.3 billion in revenue in H1 2026, a nearly fifteen-fold increase from the prior year, while reporting an $80.7 billion net loss in the same period. This filing provides the most detailed financial picture ahead of its anticipated IPO.

The substantial net loss is primarily due to non-cash accounting adjustments, with roughly $72 billion stemming from convertible notes and financing instruments. These paper charges ballooned as Anthropic's private valuation soared to $965 billion by May. The company also achieved adjusted profitability and positive free cash flow in Q3 2026.

Despite the accounting adjustments, the cash costs are significant. Anthropic spent nearly $9 billion on compute and infrastructure in the first six months of 2026, already surpassing its total spend for all of 2025. The company also boasts a strong efficiency metric, generating $1.70 in revenue for every dollar spent on compute.

Future commitments are enormous, with Anthropic locking in approximately $450 billion in cloud compute agreements over the next 7-10 years. This includes $111 billion with Google Cloud, $110 billion with Amazon Web Services, and $31 billion with Microsoft. Total committed infrastructure spending now exceeds $600 billion, with about 80% non-cancellable.

The prospectus also highlights significant risks, including customer concentration, with 20-25% of H1 revenue from just two unnamed customers without long-term contracts. Additionally, the filing includes a candid 'catastrophic incident' warning among its risk factors, acknowledging potential dangers of frontier AI development.

Anthropic has pledged to dedicate about 20% of its shares to a 'public benefit' fund to address AI's economic effects. This commitment, alongside a $200 million pledge for AI labor-market impact studies, has drawn both praise for structural innovation and skepticism from critics.
caption:
Anthropic's S-1 filing reveals a staggering $16.3 billion in H1 2026 revenue, but also an $80.7 billion net loss. The AI giant is preparing for one of the year's biggest IPOs.

topic: ai coding agents get office and browser tools
headline_marked: [[deskmates creates a pixel-art office]] to visualize your AI coding agents' work
headline: deskmates creates a pixel-art office to visualize your AI coding agents' work
summary: This new tool transforms invisible AI coding sessions into pixel-art characters in a virtual office, showing their real-time activity and when they need your input.
details: Currently, AI coding agents often work invisibly in the background, making it hard to track their progress or know when they need input. deskmates addresses this by creating a pixel-art office where each agent session is represented as a character at a desk.

These characters visually mimic agent activity: typing during edits, reading during searches, and raising a yellow question mark when user permission is required. Subagents appear next to their launchers and deliver documents upon completion.

The tool prioritizes privacy, with events carrying only a tool name and a brief detail (max 120 chars). Prompts, file contents, and tool output never leave the local adapters, and daily history stores only counts, not sensitive content.

deskmates can be served over a LAN, allowing the office visualization to be displayed on a tablet or a larger screen in kiosk mode. This ensures the pixel art remains crisp across various display sizes.

The project also features a shared office mode, enabling multiple users to relay small events to a central 'Headquarters' floor. Here, agents from different PCs can interact, even 'chatting' in a virtual café when waiting for simultaneous permissions.
caption:
Are your AI coding agents invisible? A new pixel-art office tool, deskmates, visualizes their real-time work, waits, and interactions.
